title: Multi-tier capacity scarcity sandbox and operator playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document describes the "capacity scarcity sandbox" (CSS): a reproducible, low-risk environment and operator playbook to validate, observe, and rehearse operator actions during multi-tier capacity scarcity events. The goal is to exercise throttling, prefetching, eviction, and degradation policies across tenant priority tiers (platinum/gold/silver/beta) and measure SLO impact before these changes are ever applied in production.

Why we need a sandbox

- Real production scarcity events expose complex interactions between batching, KV-prefix cache hits, model-variant fallbacks, and tenant fair-share.
- Operators need validated sequences they can run under control with predictable rollback.
- Product and SRE teams must quantify user-visible impact (tail latency, error-rate, quality regressions) for any mitigation policy.

Scope and assumptions

- Scope: platform-level capacity scarcity for inference serving runtime (gpu-pool-controller, request-router, prefix-cache, tenant-quota-manager).
- Assumes access to: a staging GPU pool (min 8 GPUs), traffic replay harness, tenant workload generator, sandbox observability stack (grafana, loki, tempo).
- Not in scope: model weight changes, long-running dataset migrations, on-prem hardware maintenance.

Key concepts and owners

- Capacity Scarcity Sandbox (CSS) environment: owner eng-platform/ops-team.
- Tenant priority tiers: defined in tenant-config-service (platinum, gold, silver, beta).
- Operator playbook lead: Aisha Patel. Oncall escalation to Platform Pager (eng-sre) if escalation threshold exceeded.

SLOs and alert thresholds used in the sandbox

- Primary SLOs (sandbox baseline):
  - P95 token latency < 120 ms for platinum tenants
  - P99 token latency < 300 ms for platinum tenants
  - Model error-rate (5xx) < 0.3%
  - Token cost per request baseline recorded for delta comparisons

- Alert thresholds (for operator training):
  - p95_platinum_latency > 150 ms for 3m -> trigger CSS_alert_high_latency
  - p99_platinum_latency > 400 ms for 5m -> trigger CSS_alert_tail_pause
  - global_token_error_rate > 1% for 2m -> CSS_alert_error_spike

Sandbox architecture (logical)

- Reused components: request-router (rr), batch-service (bs), model-gateway (mg), kv-prefix-cache (kvc), tenant-quota-manager (tqm), gpu-pool-controller (gpc).
- Traffic sources: replay harness (replay-cli), synthetic generator (workgen).
- Observability: grafana dashboards (css-ops-overview), loki for logs, tempo for traces, cost-meter for token accounting.

Table: sandbox resources and minimum config

| Component | Minimum config (staging) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPU pool | 8 x A10g equivalent | Reserve with gpc; label: css-staging |
| Request router | 3 replicas | Set CIRCUIT_BREAKER=0.8 for tests |
| Batch service | 2 replicas | Batch-size cap = 64 |
| KV prefix cache | 4 shards | Prefetch enabled in experiments |
| Tenant quota mgr | default policies | Use tier multipliers: platinum=1.0, gold=0.7, silver=0.4, beta=0.1 |

Playbook: sandbox exercise sequence (operator steps)

1) Prepare the environment (15–30m)
   - Verify GPU pool health: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=gpu-node
   - Ensure replay harness credentials and sample sets present: run replay-cli auth whoami
   - Snapshot current staging config: /opt/css/scripts/snapshot-config.sh > /tmp/css-snapshot-$(date +%s).yaml

2) Baseline run (30m)
   - Start low-volume replay (10% traffic). Command: replay-cli run --profile baseline --duration 30m --target rr-staging.internal:8080
   - Observe dashboards: open grafana/css-ops-overview -> record p95/p99, error-rate, token-cost delta.

3) Controlled scarcity ramp (1h)
   - Ramp synthetic traffic to 140% of GPU pool capacity in 4 steps: 60% -> 90% -> 110% -> 140%. Use workgen: workgen stress --target rr-staging.internal --steps 60,90,110,140 --hold 10m
   - At each step record: p95_platinum, p99_platinum, cache hit-rate, avg batch size, evicted prefix count.

4) Run mitigation scenarios (parallel branches)
   A) Soft-tier throttling (no eviction)
      - Enable per-tenant soft throttles: kubectl exec tqm -- /bin/sh -c 'tqmctl set-rate-limit --tier silver=0.5 --tier beta=0.2'
      - Monitor user-visible SLOs for platinum and gold.

   B) Prefetch handoff + KV-cohesion
      - Toggle prefetch hints: patch batch-service config prefetch.enabled=true
      - Validate cache hit-rate improves and tail latency reduces for gold tenants.

   C) Conservative eviction + reserved slots for platinum
      - Enable eviction policy in gpc: "eviction.mode=conservative" and reserve 20% slots for platinum. YAML snippet:

      ```yaml
      gpu-pool-controller:
        eviction:
          mode: conservative
          reserve_pct_for_tier:
            platinum: 0.20
            gold: 0.05
      ```

      - Apply: kubectl apply -f gpc-eviction-config.yaml
      - Observe failovers to model-variant-lightrun where applicable.

5) Quantify quality and cost tradeoffs (15–30m per scenario)
   - Run short prompt set evaluation (eval-harness) against affected tenant requests to measure quality delta (token-level divergence + rouge/spice approximations).
   - Record token-cost per successful response and compute delta vs baseline.

6) Controlled rollback and cleanup (15m)
   - Revert configs using snapshot from step 1: /opt/css/scripts/restore-config.sh /tmp/css-snapshot-*.yaml
   - Drain test traffic and confirm production-mirroring flags are off.

Operator decision matrix (when to pick a mitigation)

- If platinum p99 > 400 ms but global error-rate < 0.5% -> prefer reservation + conservative-eviction.
- If p95 degradation is modest but cache hit-rate low -> prefer prefetch handoff and batch-cohesion tuning.
- If error-rate increases alongside latency -> investigate model-gateway 5xxs (mg logs) before applying throttles.

Dashboard and alert templates

- Dashboard: css-ops-overview (panels):
  - Global token ingress by tier (time-series)
  - p95 / p99 latency by tier
  - KV prefix cache hit-rate and evictions
  - Batch size distribution and batching latency
  - GPU utilization and reserved-slot usage
  - Token-cost delta by tenant

- Alert: CSS_alert_high_latency (prometheus rule):
  - expr: avg_over_time(platinum_p95_latency[3m]) > 0.15
  - for: 3m
  - labels: severity=page, team=platform-ops
  - annotations: summary, runbook link to this page

Example Prometheus rule (YAML):

  - alert: CSS_alert_high_latency
    expr: avg_over_time(service_platinum_p95_latency_seconds[3m]) > 0.15
    for: 3m
    labels:
      severity: page
      team: platform-ops
    annotations:
      summary: "Platinum p95 latency above 150ms (sandbox threshold)"
      runbook: "confluence://eng-platform/how-tos/multi-tier-capacity-scarcity-sandbox-and-operator-playbook"

Training checklist and acceptance criteria

- Operators must be able to:
  - Stand up CSS environment in <60m using documented scripts
  - Run the full four-step scarcity ramp and collect measurement artifacts
  - Choose and apply a mitigation scenario and quantify its effect within 60m
  - Perform rollback without residual config drift

- Acceptance criteria for a successful training run:
  1. Baseline snapshot file exists and restores successfully.
  2. Metrics artifacts (CSV/JSON) uploaded to /mnt/css-artifacts for postmortem.
  3. One mitigation scenario applied and evidence of improved p99 or cost delta is recorded.

Postmortem and retrospective cadence

- After each CSS run: create a short retrospective doc using template css-retrospective-template.md and tag #css-exercise. Include: hypothesis, measurements, operator timeline, decisions, and action items.
- Quarterly: consolidate learnings into platform-roadmap input (tag: capacity-attenuation).

Safety notes and guardrails

- Do not run CSS with production credentials. Replay and workgen must target staging endpoints only.
- All gpc eviction configs must include a disable-guard value; if absent, the change is rejected by the operator CLI.
- Emergency abort: kubectl -n inference annotate gpu-pool-controller css.abort=true which triggers immediate rollback of last applied CSS patch by the operator-helper service.

Appendix: useful commands and scripts

- Snapshot staging config:
  - /opt/css/scripts/snapshot-config.sh --out /tmp/css-snapshot.yaml
- Restore:
  - /opt/css/scripts/restore-config.sh /tmp/css-snapshot.yaml
- Start baseline replay:
  - replay-cli run --profile baseline --duration 30m --target rr-staging.internal:8080
- Ramp traffic with workgen:
  - workgen stress --target rr-staging.internal --steps 60,90,110,140 --hold 10m
- Apply eviction config:
  - kubectl apply -f gpc-eviction-config.yaml -n inference
